title: Opus 5.5 or Sol 6.1?
author: camawan
selftext: Ive been using codex for the past month primarily for game dev (unity + blender) and been happy with it. With the reduced usage for codex yesterday im thinking of switching back to claude. How does opus 5.5 vs Sol 6.1 perform for game development specifically?

comments.author: Odd-Animator1265
comments.body: Wondering too. When you switch, then it looks like you will be fine with the default settings in Opus 5.5. Look for Nate Herk on YouTube. He goes through it with exempels. Might save you some tokens

comments.author: vagonblog
comments.body:
i’d test both on the same small task in a copy of your project, like fixing a unity bug or modifying a blender script. count the corrections needed and actually run the result. a convincing explanation doesn’t tell you whether the scene works.

if codex has been working well for you, the useful question is whether claude gets you to a working result with fewer retries within your budget. keep the project context and tool access comparable so you’re not accidentally comparing different setups.

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body: Can’t help but recommend opus. It has a much better understanding of what you want. That’s not to say Astra or 6.1 is necessarily bad. They’re very capable. But opus just has better implementation across the board in my experience. Astra and 6.1 can look at opus’ work and do it the same, but it can’t really come up with ideas like opus can.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
I've found having a codex plan of some kind to be invaluable due to imagegen mockups. If I had to pick one of the two, I'd go with that. Though I personally just have both. I have them focus on their strengths (Astra gens mockups for me as well as handles all review tasks to give the Opus implementers a different lens to work through. Also Astra seems to have better visual analysis, which seems to be why it's particularly good with gauntleted tasks / review loops as well as architectural modeling.

So two different use cases here. I could see an argument for just Opus if someone was just blowing tokens on one-shotting, too, as its one-shots are of higher quality. But I find that entire premise to be a waste.
